issue_text:
A real human-and-agent coding session (persona: Mind Changer) on the wodsmith competition app. Ten human prompts, three tasks:

• Change the colors — “the red and orange together are pretty hideous … make it all orange”, followed by five corrections that each move the goal: “you can't even see the red text”, “FIX THE RED TEXT FUCKING REMOVE ALL RED ON THE PAGE”, “then its text-orange-700 which does not work on the orange background”, “that looks shitty though. change it to orange background and white text” — then a request to save the work.

• Fix the layout — “the submission box on line 526 has buttons that are breaking out of the container on smaller widths” — then another save request.

• Remove a feature — “lets remove streamable as an option for athletes to submit a video link. so just youtube or vimeo”
summary:
A 10-prompt back-and-forth between a human and Claude Code on the wodsmith competition app. The human is a Mind Changer: they keep changing both what they want and what counts as done. The session has three parts:

  • The color fight (T1–T22, H1–H7). 'Make it all orange' takes six prompts to settle. The agent's first pass misses badges whose red comes from variant="destructive", and the Badge component's own default style quietly beats the orange the agent adds on top. The human's anger peaks at H4 (all-caps); the real fix only lands after the human names the exact failing class (H5).
  • The layout fix (T23–T32, H8–H9). Buttons break out of their box on small screens. The agent's editing tool fails twice because the file uses tabs instead of spaces, so the agent edits the file with a Python script instead, then re-reads the section to confirm.
  • Removing Streamable (T33–T42, H10). The cleanest part: search the whole project, edit the main schema file first, delete the leftover pieces, and finish with a final search that finds nothing.

Worth noticing:

  • At T6 the agent argues back at the human — and is later shown to be wrong.
  • At T15–T16 the human naming the exact class finally leads the agent to read the component's code and find the real cause.
  • Checking is one-sided: twice the agent declares success (T6, T13) and the human overrules it. For how-it-looks work, the human's eye is the only real check. The Streamable part, by contrast, checks itself convincingly.
  • All three parts end saved (committed), and the agent always honors 'leave db/index.ts out'.

findings.title: The human is the error signal
findings.body: Every Reflection tag in the run (T9, T15, T25) is triggered by a human complaint or a tool error — never by the agent's own checks. Both times the agent checked its own work in the styling part (T6 'contrast is good', T13 'all red removed'), the next human message overruled it. For visual work this agent has no way to check itself except the user.

findings.title: Argues back, then admits it was wrong, three turns apart
findings.body: T6 is the rare turn where the agent argues back and asks the human a question (Grounding › Ask for clarification). By T9 the quote 'you're right, the variant="destructive"… would override the className colors' (Reflection › Receive and integrate external feedback) marks the exact moment it changes its mind — visible only at the quote level.

findings.title: The real cause is found five turns after the symptom
findings.body: The unreadable badge is reported at T5, but the real cause is only found at T16, after the human names the exact class. The chain there is textbook: notice the fix did not work → form a guess → read the component's code → find the cause. The turns in between (T8–T13) fixed individual badges, not the cause.

findings.title: Invisible characters break the edit tool; recovery is step-by-step and careful
findings.body: Two failed edits (T24, T28) on a tab-indented file produce a step-by-step fallback: a command that reveals invisible characters → a Python script that does the replacement → printing the line to double-check before deleting it (Reflection › Pre-action self-check inside an action) → re-reading the whole section. The recover phase is 4 of 42 turns, all in this one part.

segments.title: Human asks for all orange · Agent changes every red to orange
segments.summary: Human asks to change the 'hideous' red penalty UI to orange (H1). Agent repeats back the request, searches for red- color classes, changes nine of them to orange, and reports it is done — without checking how it actually looks.

segments.title: Human reports an unreadable badge · Agent argues back, then fixes it
segments.summary: Human says line 442 is unreadable (H2). Agent argues back, insisting the badge is already correct (T6). Human points at two more broken lines (H3). Agent finds the shared cause — variant="destructive" makes badges red — fixes three badges, and admits 'you're right' (T9).

segments.title: Human shouts, then gives a hint · Agent finds the real cause
segments.summary: Human shouts in all-caps to remove all red (H4). Agent searches the page and finds no red left. Human then names the exact class that is not working, text-orange-700 (H5). Agent guesses the Badge component is overriding the color, reads its code, finds the real cause — the component's built-in white text wins over the orange — and fixes it with variant="outline" (T15–T16).

segments.title: Human picks new colors · Agent restyles and saves
segments.summary: Human dislikes the result and asks for solid orange with white text (H6). Agent applies it without comment (T19). Human asks to save the work but leave out db/index.ts (H7). Agent saves (commits) only the page file.

segments.title: Human reports a broken layout · Agent recovers from failed edits
segments.summary: Human says the buttons break out of their box on small screens (H8). Agent finds the cause and rewrites the layout as a two-column grid; its editing tool fails twice because the file uses tabs, not spaces (T24, T28), so agent switches to editing the file with a Python script, then re-reads the section to make sure it is right. Human asks to save (H9); agent commits.

segments.title: Human removes an option · Agent deletes it everywhere
segments.summary: Human asks to remove Streamable so athletes can only submit YouTube or Vimeo links (H10). Agent searches the whole project, edits the main schema file first, removes the player code and the now-unused BasicEmbed component, cleans up the server-side check, and proves it is done with a final search that finds nothing.
